name: Bill Gates
description: A journey through opportunities, calculated risks, and defining decisions that shaped a life of technology and purpose — but every choice can lead you to a completely different fate.

scoring.historicalSimilarity: sum of weight for historically matching choices / sum of all event weights * 100
scoring.risk: average risk score of selected choices
scoring.independence: average independence score of selected choices

events.title: The Computing Machine
events.playerFact: Your school gains access to a rare computing machine — an expensive device that almost no one your age has ever touched. You become fascinated by the idea that you can tell this machine what to do through code.
events.historicalFact: As a teenager, you gained access to a computer terminal and became deeply interested in programming, spending countless hours learning to write code.
events.question: Do you spend your free time learning programming?

yes.consequence: You become fascinated by programming and spend as much time as possible experimenting with the machine.

no.consequence: You decide these machines are just a hobby and focus your attention on regular studies.

events.title: The Companion
events.playerFact: At school, you meet someone who is just as obsessed with computing machines as you are. The two of you begin spending every possible moment together, writing programs, exploring systems, and dreaming about what these machines could become.
events.historicalFact: At school you met a kindred spirit who shared your passion for computers — a friendship that would grow into one of the most important partnerships in technology.
events.question: Do you collaborate with this companion on projects?

yes.consequence: You and your new friend begin spending countless hours writing programs together.

no.consequence: You keep your programming projects mostly to yourself and work alone.

events.title: Real-World Experience
events.playerFact: While still in school, you and your friend find opportunities to work with real computing systems for local organizations. You write actual code that businesses use — an extraordinary experience for someone your age.
events.historicalFact: You and your friend gained early programming experience through real-world projects for local companies.
events.question: Do you accept this opportunity to work with real systems?

yes.consequence: You gain valuable experience working with real-world systems while still a student.

no.consequence: You decide to focus on school and wait until you are older to enter the workforce.

events.title: Famous University
events.playerFact: You are accepted into one of the most prestigious universities in the world. Your family expects you to go, and it is a remarkable opportunity — but it means leaving behind the practical work you love.
events.historicalFact: You enrolled at Harvard University in 1973, where you studied mathematics and computer science.
events.question: Do you drop out of university and jump straight into entrepreneurship?

yes.consequence: You skip university and immediately pursue opportunities in the technology industry — a big risk but an adventurous one.

no.consequence: You move to the university town and begin studying while continuing to think about technology.

events.title: The New Device
events.playerFact: You learn about a new personal computing device that has just been announced — a machine for hobbyists. It has no software. You and your friend realize you could write a programming language for it. It is a gamble, but it could be the beginning of something much bigger.
events.historicalFact: You learned about one of the first personal computers and you and your friend built a version of the BASIC programming language for it, launching your software company.
events.question: Do you build the software for this device?

yes.consequence: You and your partner build a programming language and see an opportunity in the emerging market.

no.consequence: You decide the machine is too limited and wait for more powerful devices.

events.title: Leaving University
events.playerFact: Your software business is growing. You have real customers and real revenue. But you are still enrolled at the most prestigious university in the country. You cannot do both at full capacity.
events.historicalFact: You left university without completing your degree to focus full-time on the software company you had co-founded — a decision that would prove transformative.
events.question: Do you leave university and pursue the company full-time?

yes.consequence: You leave university and dedicate yourself completely to building the software company.

no.consequence: You stay at university and try to build the company while completing your education — but both remain incomplete.

events.title: The Giant Corporation
events.playerFact: The largest technology company in the world is building a new personal device. They need software — specifically, an operating system. They come to your small company. This is the opportunity of a lifetime.
events.historicalFact: IBM approached your young company about providing software for its new personal computer. You supplied an operating system that would become the foundation of a computing empire.
events.question: Do you refuse to work with this giant company?

yes.consequence: You decide that working with such a large company is too risky and turn down the offer.

no.consequence: You pursue the deal and secure an opportunity to put your software on a major new device.

events.title: Keeping the Rights
events.playerFact: The deal is on the table. The large company wants your operating system, but they want to license it exclusively. Your instinct tells you something different: keep the ability to sell it to everyone else.
events.historicalFact: You licensed the operating system to the computer giant while retaining the right to license it to other manufacturers — a decision that made your software the industry standard.
events.question: Do you retain the right to license to others?

yes.consequence: You retain the ability to license the operating system to other manufacturers, allowing the software business to expand.

no.consequence: You give the major company exclusive control and build your business around one hardware partner — safer but more limiting.

events.title: Visual Interface
events.playerFact: Computers are evolving from text-based machines to something visual. You see that the future of personal computing is graphical — windows, icons, menus, and a pointing device. You pour resources into building a graphical system.
events.historicalFact: You bet the company on a graphical operating system, releasing the first version of Windows and laying the foundation for decades of dominance in personal computing.
events.question: Do you stay loyal to old text-based software and avoid graphics?

yes.consequence: You continue focusing on text-based software and leave graphical computing to competitors.

no.consequence: You invest heavily in graphical computing and pursue a future of visual operating systems.

events.title: Another Purpose
events.playerFact: You have led your company to extraordinary success. You are one of the wealthiest people in the world. But you increasingly feel that your real impact could be somewhere else — saving lives, improving health, solving problems that technology alone cannot fix.
events.historicalFact: You stepped down as CEO of your company in 2000 and turned your focus to philanthropy, creating one of the largest charitable foundations in the world.
events.question: Do you step away from running your company and focus more on philanthropy?

yes.consequence: You step back from day-to-day leadership and dedicate much of your time and resources to philanthropy, building a legacy beyond technology.

no.consequence: You remain focused on technology and continue directing the company yourself, but the bigger questions about your purpose never leave you.

events.title: The Model Employee
events.playerFact: You abandon computing machines and turn to ordinary studies and a normal life. You become a diligent clerk in a government office.
events.historicalFact: Many of your talented contemporaries, by not pursuing technology opportunities, remained in ordinary jobs.
events.question: Are you satisfied with this quiet, carefree life?

yes.consequence: You spend years in the office, retire, and live an average life. You never impact the world, but your conscience is clear.

no.consequence: You grow to hate this life and chase your old dreams — but time is lost, and you never reach the top.

events.title: Late Regret
events.playerFact: In middle age, you see the news about the technology revolution. Those who were once your classmates have changed the world, and you are left on the sidelines.
events.historicalFact: Success stories in technology are full of people who took risks at the right time.
events.question: Do you regret abandoning that computing machine?

yes.consequence: You look back with regret and decide to write a book about your memories. It becomes a bestseller, turning you into a successful author.

no.consequence: You die content, believing a quiet life was better than the anxieties of entrepreneurship — unaware that the world will never remember your name.

events.title: The Lone Programmer
events.playerFact: You reject your companion and continue programming alone. You build small projects but never form a powerful partnership.
events.historicalFact: Some talented programmers, due to a lack of collaboration, never turned big ideas into big products.
events.question: Are you satisfied with working alone?

yes.consequence: You become an independent developer, writing useful software, but you never build an empire.

no.consequence: You constantly think about that lost companion, and this regret haunts you for the rest of your life.

events.title: Unknown Among Giants
events.playerFact: While others build large technology companies, you still work as an independent developer. You have respect, but fame and fortune never come.
events.historicalFact: The history of technology is filled with hidden talents who never achieved fame.
events.question: Are you satisfied with this anonymity?

yes.consequence: You live peacefully, knowing you did your work right, even though the world never knew you.

no.consequence: You watch others' progress with regret, constantly wishing you had built a powerful partnership instead of going it alone.

events.title: The Diligent Student
events.playerFact: You abandon practical projects and focus on school and university studies. You get excellent grades and are recognized as a model student.
events.historicalFact: Many talented students, by prioritizing grades over practical experience, never fulfilled their potential.
events.question: Do you continue on this academic path?

yes.consequence: You graduate, become a university professor, and have a quiet academic life, but you never bring a product to market.

no.consequence: You drop out halfway and seek practical work, but time is lost and you've lost your competitive edge.

events.title: The Forgotten Professor
events.playerFact: You teach at the university for years and publish mediocre papers. Your students remember you as a precise but uninspiring professor.
events.historicalFact: The history of science and technology forgets the cautious and only remembers the bold.
events.question: Do you regret choosing the academic path?

yes.consequence: You live with regret, wishing you had built a great product instead of just teaching.

no.consequence: You live peacefully, believing the university was a worthy place for you, though the world never felt your impact.

events.title: The Young Entrepreneur
events.playerFact: You leave university and jump straight into the world of entrepreneurship. But without enough experience and without the right partner, your company quickly goes bankrupt.
events.historicalFact: Many young entrepreneurs, despite talent, failed at their first attempt due to lack of preparation and lack of the right partnership.
events.question: Do you learn from this failure and try again?

yes.consequence: You learn from failure, form a new partnership, and this time succeed — though later than your competitors.

no.consequence: You give up on entrepreneurship and take a regular job. Years later, seeing others' success, you regret it.

events.title: The Late Bloomer
events.playerFact: With a new partnership, you start a small business. You have some success, but never reach the scale of your larger competitors. You are always a step behind.
events.historicalFact: Business history shows that timing is as important as the idea.
events.question: Are you satisfied with your moderate success?

yes.consequence: You live with pride, knowing you built something from your initial failure, even if you never reached the summit.

no.consequence: You live with regret, always wondering what would have happened if you hadn't left university at that time.

events.title: Spectator of the Revolution
events.playerFact: You reject the new personal device and wait for more advanced technology. But the market fills up quickly, and the golden opportunity slips away.
events.historicalFact: Many large companies of that era ignored the personal computer market and missed a historic opportunity.
events.question: Do you regret not entering the market earlier?

yes.consequence: Years later, when personal devices become ubiquitous, you enter but have lost your competitive position.

no.consequence: You never enter this market and continue working in more traditional fields, though you miss out on big opportunities.

events.title: Left Behind by History
events.playerFact: The world is changing rapidly and you are left on the sidelines. The large companies that were once small are now giants, and you are just a spectator.
events.historicalFact: The history of technology is full of those who didn't take risks and lost their opportunities.
events.question: Do you wish you had taken the risk and entered the game?

yes.consequence: You live with regret, wishing you had chosen courage over caution.

no.consequence: You live content, believing caution saved you from big failures — unaware that you also lost big opportunities.

events.title: Stuck in Between
events.playerFact: You decide to both continue university and build the company. But you are not fully committed to either. Both remain incomplete.
events.historicalFact: Some entrepreneurs, due to a lack of focus, failed to pursue either path well and failed.
events.question: Do you continue on the dual path?

yes.consequence: You remain in this duality for years, earn your degree but your company stays small, and you never achieve great success.

no.consequence: You choose one, but it's too late; you've fallen behind in both, and neither succeeds.

events.title: Persistent Frustration
events.playerFact: Your peers have either become prominent professors or great entrepreneurs. You have become neither. You are left in a middle ground that is neither this nor that.
events.historicalFact: History forgets the middle-grounders and only rewards the peak-dwellers.
events.question: Do you wish you had chosen one path full-time?

yes.consequence: You live with regret, wishing you had focused on one goal instead of being torn between two.

no.consequence: You live bitterly, blaming circumstances, but deep down you know it was your own fault.

events.title: The Missed Opportunity
events.playerFact: You turn down the giant corporation's offer. A few years later, that same corporation partners with someone else, and that someone becomes an industry giant. You are left regretting the missed opportunity.
events.historicalFact: In the history of technology, turning down a big offer sometimes means losing an entire industry.
events.question: Do you regret this decision?

yes.consequence: You live for years with this regret and never forgive yourself for letting that opportunity slip away.

no.consequence: You pass by the matter indifferently and continue with smaller projects, but you know you ignored a historic opportunity.

events.title: Bitter Memories
events.playerFact: Every time you hear the name of that giant corporation and its new partner, your heart sinks. You know you could have been in their place, but you weren't.
events.historicalFact: History forgets hesitant people and remembers only those who took risks.
events.question: Do you carry this regret with you forever?

yes.consequence: You live with an agonizing regret, wishing in your last breath you had chosen courage over fear.

no.consequence: You live bitterly, telling yourself it was fate — but deep down, you know it was your own fault.

events.title: The Exclusive Partner
events.playerFact: You give exclusive rights to the giant company. In the short term, you have good deals, but when that company moves to another manufacturer, your business collapses.
events.historicalFact: Business history is full of companies that became dependent on one large partner and were later destroyed.
events.question: Do you regret this dependency?

yes.consequence: With the company's collapse, you lose everything. Years later, you regret not keeping the rights for yourself.

no.consequence: Despite the failure, you don't blame yourself, believing you made the best decision at the time — even though it led to ruin.

events.title: Collapse
events.playerFact: Your company no longer exists. You are a failed entrepreneur who, with one wrong decision, lost all your capital.
events.historicalFact: The history of technology is full of entrepreneurs who, with one wrong decision, fell from the peak to the bottom.
events.question: Do you wish you had signed that contract differently?

yes.consequence: You live with regret, wishing in your final moments you had thought about the long-term future instead of short-term security.

no.consequence: You live bitterly, telling yourself it was fate — but you know you destroyed your own future.

events.title: Loyal to Text
events.playerFact: You reject graphical interfaces and continue with text-based software. Your competitors, with visual systems, capture the market and you fall behind.
events.historicalFact: Some software companies, by failing to accept graphical interfaces, were eliminated from the market.
events.question: Do you regret this loyalty to old methods?

yes.consequence: Years later, when everyone has moved to graphics, you enter but it's too late, and you've lost market share.

no.consequence: You remain loyal to text-based software until the end, keeping a small niche of customers — but you never grow.

events.title: Survivor of the Text Era
events.playerFact: While the world moves toward images and interaction, you still cling to old methods. Your company is small and getting smaller.
events.historicalFact: The history of technology is a graveyard of companies that couldn't adapt to change.
events.question: Do you wish you had moved toward graphics in time?

yes.consequence: You live with regret, wishing you had been more flexible and seen the future sooner instead of being stubborn.

no.consequence: You live with pride, believing you preserved the correctness of your methods, even though the world moved on without you.

events.title: Global Philanthropy
events.playerFact: After stepping down from the company, you have become one of history's greatest philanthropists. You have spent hundreds of millions of dollars fighting disease and poverty in developing countries. Your name is recorded alongside the world's greatest humanitarians.
events.historicalFact: Bill Gates, after leaving Microsoft's day-to-day management, founded the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation with his wife.
events.question: Are you satisfied with a life devoted to philanthropy?

yes.consequence: You live with deep peace, knowing your legacy is not just software but lives saved.

no.consequence: You regret leaving the technology world behind, wishing you had continued to innovate instead of turning to philanthropy.

events.title: The Enduring Tech Leader
events.playerFact: Despite the pressures, you stay with the company and lead it to new successes. Though the big questions about your purpose never leave you.
events.historicalFact: Some technology founders never stepped away from day-to-day management and led their companies until the end.
events.question: Are you satisfied with continuing to develop the company instead of changing the world in other ways?

yes.consequence: You live with pride, knowing your company continued to grow and innovate, even if your impact was limited to the technology industry.

no.consequence: You live with deep regret, wishing you had sought a new mission instead of following the old path.

events.title: Bestselling Author
events.playerFact: Regretting the lost computing machine, you decide to write your memoirs. The book quickly becomes a bestseller, turning you into a popular motivational speaker. Now many young people draw inspiration from your experience.
events.historicalFact: Some former employees of technology companies gained fame by writing memoirs.
events.question: Do you enjoy your new life as an author and speaker?

yes.consequence: You live with satisfaction, knowing that even though you didn't achieve great success yourself, you've inspired young people to take risks.

no.consequence: You live regretting the lost days, wishing you had taken the big risks yourself like the heroes in your books.

events.title: Open-Source Pioneer
events.playerFact: You continued programming alone but decided to release your work for free. A large community of developers around the world uses your code, and you are recognized as a founding figure in the open-source movement.
events.historicalFact: Some unknown programmers, by creating open-source projects, had a profound impact on the software industry.
events.question: Are you satisfied with this global impact, despite your anonymity?

yes.consequence: You live with pride, knowing that even without money or fame, your code runs worldwide and has affected millions of lives.

no.consequence: You live regretting the lost wealth and fame, wishing you had commercialized your work.

events.title: Independent Tech Consultant
events.playerFact: Despite your anonymity, you work as a senior consultant for small companies and startups. Your deep experience has made you one of the best in the industry. Your income is good, but your name is still not widely known.
events.historicalFact: Some experienced developers, by passing on their knowledge, became successful consultants.
events.question: Are you satisfied with this hidden influential role?

yes.consequence: You live peacefully, knowing you have a deep impact on the future of technology, even if you remain in the shadows.

no.consequence: You live regretting not being seen, wishing you had built a large company instead of consulting.

events.title: Technology Management Theorist
events.playerFact: By staying in academia, you have become one of the most prominent theorists of technology management. Your books are taught in business schools, and policymakers seek your advice.
events.historicalFact: Some university professors, through research on innovation, became influential figures in technology policy.
events.question: Do you enjoy influencing policy over building products?

yes.consequence: You live with pride, knowing your ideas have shaped national technology development strategies.

no.consequence: You live regretting not implementing your ideas, wishing you had entered the field of entrepreneurship yourself.

events.title: Senior Government Advisor
events.playerFact: After years of teaching, you are appointed as a senior technology advisor to the government. You now influence national digital policy. Though unknown to the public, you are one of the most powerful figures behind the scenes.
events.historicalFact: Some university professors, by entering government, left a lasting impact on technology laws.
events.question: Are you satisfied with this hidden power?

yes.consequence: You live with pride, knowing your decisions have shaped the country's digital infrastructure.

no.consequence: You live regretting the lost creativity, wishing you had continued free innovation instead of policy.

events.title: Venture Capitalist
events.playerFact: After the relative success of your second company, you enter the scene as a venture capitalist. You identify and support dozens of startups, several of which become tech giants. Your name is now among the best in the industry.
events.historicalFact: Some successful entrepreneurs, after selling their companies, turned to investing in startups.
events.question: Do you enjoy helping others build their dreams as an investor?

yes.consequence: You live with pride, knowing your support has helped grow the technology ecosystem.

no.consequence: You live regretting the active entrepreneurship days, wishing you were building again.

events.title: Management Author
events.playerFact: Your experiences of failure and success have inspired several bestselling books on management and entrepreneurship. You are now recognized as a prominent business thinker.
events.historicalFact: Some entrepreneurs, by writing about their experiences, became influential figures in management.
events.question: Are you satisfied with teaching others instead of building companies?

yes.consequence: You live with pride, knowing your ideas have nurtured a new generation of entrepreneurs.

no.consequence: You live regretting not acting, wishing you had built a new company instead of writing.

events.title: Late Angel Investor
events.playerFact: Despite missing the early opportunity, with the capital you saved, you enter as an angel investor and invest in several successful startups. Though you came late, you've compensated.
events.historicalFact: Some investors, despite coming late, with good judgment, gained great wealth.
events.question: Are you satisfied that you arrived late but reached your goal?

yes.consequence: You accept the past and enjoy your investments, knowing you came to the right path even if late.

no.consequence: You live regretting the lost days, always thinking what greatness you could have built if you had entered earlier.

events.title: Late Partnership
events.playerFact: Despite regretting your solo path, you team up with a young developer in middle age and start a small startup. This time, balanced partnership brings moderate but satisfying success.
events.historicalFact: Some lone developers, by partnering later in life, achieved notable success.
events.question: Are you satisfied with this late partnership and moderate success?

yes.consequence: You live with pride, knowing that even though you came late, you finally understood the value of collaboration and left a small mark.

no.consequence: You live regretting the lost peak, wishing you had chosen partnership from the start.
